lessons.title: சித்திரை to பங்குனி — Tamil's own solar calendar
lessons.headword: சித்திரை வைகாசி ஆனி ஆடி ஆவணி புரட்டாசி ஐப்பசி கார்த்திகை மார்கழி தை மாசி பங்குனி
lessons.romanization: Chithirai Vaikāsi Āṉi Āḍi Āvaṇi Puraṭṭāsi Aippasi Kārthigai Mārgazhi Thai Māsi Panguṉi
lessons.gloss: the twelve months of the Tamil solar calendar — Tamil's OWN calendar, distinct from both the Gregorian and Hindu lunisolar systems

segments.text: By now you've seen Arabic and Hindi each juggle two calendars. Tamil adds a third distinct system to the mix — one still actively used for Tamil New Year and Pongal, not a historical curiosity.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: The twelve Tamil months

segments.text: சித்திரை, வைகாசி, ஆனி, ஆடி, ஆவணி, புரட்டாசி, ஐப்பசி, கார்த்திகை, மார்கழி, தை, மாசி, பங்குனி (Chithirai, Vaikāsi, Āṉi, Āḍi, Āvaṇi, Puraṭṭāsi, Aippasi, Kārthigai, Mārgazhi, Thai, Māsi, Panguṉi).

This is the Tamil solar calendar — a real, independent civil calendar, distinct from both the Gregorian calendar and the Hindu lunisolar (Vikram Samvat–style) calendar. Its months are traditionally tied to nakshatras (the 27 lunar-mansion star groups): each month is named for the nakshatra the moon sits near on the full-moon (pournami) day that falls within that month — the moon's position, not the sun's, and tied to that month's full moon specifically, not simply the month's start.

blocks.title: Why it's said this way: Be honest: this is a THIRD calendar, not a variant of the others

segments.text: You've now met three genuinely separate calendar traditions: the Gregorian solar calendar (borrowed names, everyday civil use in most of the world), the pan-Indian Hindu lunisolar calendar (Chaitra, Vaishākh... tied to the six ṛtu), and now Tamil's own solar calendar, following neither. சித்திரை 1 (the 1st of Chithirai) is Tamil New Year; தை 1 (the 1st of Thai) is Pongal, one of Tamil Nadu's most important harvest festivals. These dates are fixed by the Tamil solar calendar, and only shift slightly against the Gregorian calendar (rather than drifting widely, the way lunar/lunisolar festival dates do) because it's solar too — just a different solar calendar, starting its year at a different point and naming its months differently.

segments.instruction: the twelve — "Chithirai, Vaikāsi, Āṉi, Āḍi, Āvaṇi, Puraṭṭāsi, Aippasi, Kārthigai, Mārgazhi, Thai, Māsi, Panguṉi"
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the twelve — "Chithirai, Vaikāsi, Āṉi, Āḍi, Āvaṇi, Puraṭṭāsi, Aippasi, Kārthigai, Mārgazhi, Thai, Māsi, Panguṉi"]

segments.instruction: "Chithirai 1" — Tamil New Year
"Thai 1" — Pongal

segments.text: What kind of calendar is the Tamil month system — solar, lunar, or lunisolar? (Solar — a genuinely separate calendar from both Gregorian and Hindu lunisolar.) What are the twelve months traditionally named for? (Nakshatras, lunar-mansion star groups.) What two important occasions are dated by this calendar? (Tamil New Year (Chithirai 1) and Pongal (Thai 1).)

lessons.title: ம (ma) — upright on the left, curve on the right
lessons.gloss: the single letter ம — met, then written

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach them, but leave these sections until you have stopped: Script you'll notice: ம and Guided Practice.

segments.text: Before the new one: say the sound of க.
One letter this time. Just one.

One unbroken stroke again, like வ. The only thing to get right is which way round it goes: the upright is on the LEFT and the curve on the right. Most people guess the reverse, because that is the habit Devanagari teaches — hanging a shape off a right-hand spine.
ம — ma.
What it is made of:
a straight vertical stroke on the LEFT.
a horizontal along the bottom.
a rounded arch closing it on the RIGHT.
It is the last consonant of வணக்கம்.
1. start at the top left and draw the left upright straight DOWN to the baseline.
2. without lifting, turn right and run along the bottom to the far right.
3. without lifting, turn up and rise up the right side.
4. without lifting, curve over the top and back towards the left.
5. without lifting, come down the middle to the bottom bar — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 0. The pen never leaves the paper.

Stroke order is one attested teaching order, not a national standard — Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation. Source: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 1 (Univ. of Texas at Austin).

lessons.title: ஆம் (ām) — writing a word that starts with a vowel
lessons.gloss: a word that begins with a vowel gets a full vowel letter, not a sign

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
waitUntilStopped: Script you'll notice: a vowel standing alone
Script you'll notice: build the word
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach them, but leave these sections until you have stopped: Script you'll notice: a vowel standing alone, Script you'll notice: build the word and Guided Practice.

segments.text: Every vowel sign so far has hooked onto a consonant — the ி on ற. This word has no consonant to hook onto.

blocks.title: Script you'll notice: a vowel standing alone

segments.text: Tamil writes a vowel two ways, and which one you use depends on where it sits:

utterances: inside a word, after a consonant, a small sign — ி in றி.
starting a word, with nothing before it, a full independent letter.

segments.text: ஆ is the independent letter for long ā. It is not a sign and never hangs off anything; it is a letter in its own right.
Long ā is short அ plus a tail, so அ is where it starts — and you have not been shown that one yet. Its parts, then the tail:
a curl at the upper left.
a long horizontal stroke.
a straight vertical on the right — that is அ.
a tail added on the right — and now it is ஆ (ā).
Those are the parts in writing order. Where the pen lifts is not settled: Tamil handwriting varies by region and by school, and this book only claims a pen path where it has a sourced one.
That is a rule, not a special case: any Tamil word that opens on a vowel opens with a full vowel letter.

blocks.title: Script you'll notice: build the word

utterances: piece: ஆ, ā, this lesson — independent.
piece: ம், m — ம (ma) with the puḷḷi, the dot you already know.

segments.text: ஆ, ம் becomes ஆம் (ām).
Two pieces only. The puḷḷi on ம் closes the word on a bare m, exactly as it did at the end of வணக்கம்.

segments.instruction: அ — curl, horizontal, right vertical
ஆ (ā) — the same three parts, then the right-hand tail
segments.source: [YOU WRITE: **ஆ** — the same three parts, then the right-hand tail]

segments.instruction: ம் — ம (ma) with the dot
ஆம் (ām) — two pieces, left to right
segments.source: [YOU WRITE: **ஆம்** — two pieces, left to right]

segments.text: Write ஆம் (ām). When does a Tamil vowel get a full letter instead of a sign? (When it starts a word — nothing precedes it to hook onto.) What closes the word? (ம் — the puḷḷi on ம (ma).) Next: noon and midnight.

lessons.title: ஆ (ā) — one character, met inside words you already say
lessons.gloss: the single character ஆ — recognised inside words you already say

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach them, but leave these sections until you have stopped: Script you'll notice: ஆ and Guided Practice.

segments.text: Before the new one: அ — what does it do?
One character this time. Just one — and you have been saying it for pages without knowing which mark on the page it was.
ஆ — ā.
It is an independent vowel — the shape the vowel ā takes when a word begins with it, rather than the sign it becomes inside a word.
What it is made of:
the whole of அ.
a tail added on the right.
You already say these, and every one of them has ஆ (ā) somewhere inside it:
ஆம் — yes (ām).
ஆம் / இல்லை / சரி ām / illai / sari — answering in Tamil.
ஆறு ஏழு பத்து āṟu ēḻu pattu — six, seven, and ten stay family cousins while Kannada regularly softens p to h.
ஆம் ām — a word that begins with a vowel gets a full vowel letter.
1. start inside the upper curl and sweep around it.
2. without lifting, continue down the outer curve.
3. without lifting, turn around the lower loop.
4. without lifting, carry the horizontal to the right edge.
5. without lifting, climb the right upright from there to its top.
6. without lifting, draw the upright down over that ink.
7. without lifting, continue into the long-vowel loop, curve right and around the bottom, then finish inside — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 0. The pen never leaves the paper.

One continuous stroke — seven joined movements, no pen lift; it goes up the right upright from the horizontal and back down it into the long-vowel loop; order from Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Frame 4, ஆ (ā), with the stroke count from native writers' pen traces in HP Labs India's LipiTk Tamil recognizer, class 1.

This is one attested teaching order and not a national standard — handwriting here is taught with school-to-school variation. Source: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 4, ஆ (ā) (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 192. The stroke count comes from native writers' pen traces in HP Labs India's LipiTk Tamil recognizer: most of them write ஆ (ā) without lifting the pen.

Is this a variant of the Hindu lunisolar calendar? (No: it is Tamil's own solar calendar, a third system beside that one and the Gregorian.)
Which day is Tamil New Year, and which is Pongal? (Chithirai 1; Thai 1.)
Which side of ம (ma) is the upright on? (The left, with the curve on the right.)
Why does ஆம் (ām) open with ஆ rather than the sign ◌ா? (The word starts on a vowel, so the vowel takes its full letter; the sign needs a consonant to hang from.)
What is ஆ (ā) made of? (The whole of அ, plus a tail on the right.)
Which two pieces build ஆம் (ām)? (ஆ, ம்: the puḷḷi closes it on a bare m.)
